Topic: Unlocking Conic Sections: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres

Target audience: High school students interested in geometry and visual mathematics

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Warm-up: The Cutting Plane

Lecture lines:
Meet the double cone and the cutting plane.
Conic sections emerge from this simple intersection.
Imagine slicing a carrot at various angles.
Circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas are formed.
The angle determines the final geometric shape.

Planned animations:
Fade in a cone and a plane intersecting to form an ellipse. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Flash the plane to emphasize the intersection angle. (Color: #FF00FF)
Draw a normal vector to the plane to show orientation. (Color: #FFFF00)

Section: section_2 — Introducing the Dandelin Spheres

Lecture lines:
Meet Dandelin spheres inside our double cone.
They touch the cone in a circular ring.
They also touch our cutting plane perfectly.

Planned animations:
Introduce two Dandelin spheres tangent to the cone. (Color: #00FFFF)
Highlight the tangent points of the spheres on the cone. (Color: #00FF00)
Fade in the ellipse curve at the intersection. (Color: #FF0000)

Section: section_3 — Visualizing the Ellipse

Lecture lines:
The plane cuts through one cone nappe.
Two spheres touch the cone and plane.
Distance sum to tangency points remains constant.

Planned animations:
Draw two lines from ellipse points to the focal spheres. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Animate a point moving along the ellipse. (Color: #FF9900)
Show the constant sum property visually with segment labels. (Color: #FFFFFF)

Section: section_4 — Parabolas and Hyperbolas

Lecture lines:
Angle changes create parabolas and hyperbolas.
Parallel edges create the unique parabola shape.
Cutting both nappes forms the beautiful hyperbola.

Planned animations:
Rotate the plane to intersect the cone edge for parabola. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Rotate the plane steeply to form hyperbola branches. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Flash both resulting shapes to highlight the difference. (Color: #00FFFF)

Section: section_5 — Summary and Geometric Elegance

Lecture lines:
Dandelin spheres bridge 3D space to 2D geometry.
These shapes underpin our physical universe.
Mathematical elegance defines orbits and satellite dishes.

Planned animations:
Fade out all previous shapes to simplify the view. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Overlay the ellipse, parabola, and hyperbola together. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight the core Dandelin sphere principle for all. (Color: #FF00FF)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: The Cutting Plane", [

            "Imagine slicing a carrot at various angles.", 
            "Circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas are formed.", 
            "The angle determines the final geometric shape."
        ])
        
        # Mobjects

        plane = Square(side_length=2, fill_opacity=0.5, color=WHITE).rotate(PI/4, axis=UP).rotate(PI/6, axis=LEFT)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Geometric Elegance", [
            "Dandelin spheres bridge 3D space to 2D geometry.",
            "These shapes underpin our physical universe.",
            "Mathematical elegance defines orbits and satellite dishes."
        ])
        
        # Create shapes
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=2, height=1, color=BLUE)
        parabola = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5*x**2, x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color=GREEN)
        hyperbola = VGroup(
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1/x, x_range=[0.5, 2], color=RED),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1/x, x_range=[-2, -0.5], color=RED)
        )
        
        shapes = VGroup(ellipse, parabola, hyperbola).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fading in (implicit start) and text highlight
        self.play(Write(shapes), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_in_area(shapes, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere, 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
